description: MAFFT 7.505 (Katoh & Standley 2013, MBE 30:772; mafft [--anysymbol] [options] in.fa), ported step by step from the program's source, for ANY number of sequences: the progressive strategies FFT-NS-2 (default), FFT-NS-1 (retree 1), NW-NS-2 (fft false) and NW-NS-1 (fft false, retree 1; retree 3 builds the guide tree three times). The pipeline is the program's (script mafft -> disttbfast): the alphabet is guessed from the letters (nucleotide when more than 75 % of the letters are A, C, G, T, U or N; sequenceType 'nuc' / 'amino' forces it); with anySymbol letters outside the alphabet - digits, '*', '#', B, Z, J, O, U in proteins - are aligned as X (n for nucleotides) and restored in the output (the plain command stops on them), '-' characters of the input are removed; the distance of two sequences is the number of shared 6-mers (10-mers with tupleSize 10, nucleotides only; amino acids in the six classes of the program) scaled by the lengths, the guide tree is the UPGMA of MAFFT (mixed linkage: treeMixing 0.1 of average and 0.9 of minimum linkage; 1 = --averagelinkage, 0 = --minimumlinkage) with the weights of the sequences from the branch lengths (unweight switches them off), the groups are aligned by the fast Fourier transform of Falign (the polarity and volume of the amino acids, the letter 'a' of nucleotides: 20 candidate shifts, windows with a high score as anchors, a chain of anchors, the segments between them aligned by the dynamic program) when fft is true, and by the group-group dynamic program A__align (gap penalties scaled by the gap frequencies of the columns of the two groups, history of the profiles of the children for groups of more than 20 sequences; legacyGapPenalty = --leavegappyregion switches the scaling off) or the dynamic program G__align11 for two single sequences; for retree 2 the distances are then recomputed from the first alignment, a second tree is built and the sequences are aligned again. Scoring = the BLOSUM matrix (bl 30, 45, 50, 62 = default, 80, 90, 100 or 0), the JTT or the transmembrane PAM matrix (scoringModel 'jtt' / 'tm' with pam steps, default 200) rescaled to 600 / mean diagonal with the offset (ep) subtracted, for nucleotides the Kimura matrix (kappa 2, 200 PAM; pam sets the distance; frequencyModel uses the letter frequencies of the data; wildcardN scores n like a wildcard) with IUPAC codes by averaging; gap opening penalty op (default 1.53, scaled by 0.6, or 1.8 for nucleotides, to an integer; opdist = --opdist for the distance step), gap extension exp (default 0), free end gaps unless terminalGapPenalty. maxIterate > 0 = FFT-NS-i / NW-NS-i (--maxiterate): the alignment of the progressive step is refined by dvtditr: dndpre computes the distances of the alignment (written with three decimals, as the file hat2 holds them), the UPGMA tree of these distances (with the branch weights of the unrooted tree: the weight of a sequence seen from a branch is the product of the weights of the branches between them) defines the branches; the alignment is cut at the windows of 20 columns whose average column score is above 0.65 x 600 (anchors) and every piece is refined: for each branch of the tree, forward and backward in turn, the two groups it separates are re-aligned (Falign with the groups' own columns as anchors; the score of the groups is the sum of pairs with the penalty once per gap) and the new alignment is kept when its score is not lower (cut-off 0, cooling); the refinement stops when 2 x n branches in a row do not change or the score oscillates, or after maxIterate cycles. reorder returns the sequences in the order of the guide tree (--reorder). thread is accepted: the program's alignment does not depend on it; its progress text with threads is thread-order dependent and is written as of one thread. The result carries the program's standard error (the banner lines of disttbfast and the strategy text of the script) unless quiet. pairLibrary 'global' / 'local' / 'genaf' (--globalpair / --localpair / --genafpair, with maxIterate 0 = G-INS-1 / L-INS-1 / E-INS-1; tbfast with pairlocalalign): (with maxIterate > 0 = G-INS-i / L-INS-i / E-INS-i the alignment is then refined by dvtditr with the constraints of the library: tbfast writes the pair library to the files hat3 (blocks, five decimals) and hat2 (distances, three decimals), dvtditr takes the UPGMA tree of hat2, and every branch is re-aligned by Falign_localhom with partA__align, whose match scores include the importance of the library blocks of the sequences of the two groups; a new alignment is kept when the sum of pairs plus the importance of the diagonal is not lower) every pair of sequences is aligned first (global alignment G__align11, local alignment L__align11 of Smith-Waterman type with cells below -offset restarting, or the local alignment with generalised affine gap costs genL__align11 with a second, dearer opening genafOpen), the distance of a pair is 2 x (1 - score / the smaller self score), the UPGMA tree of these distances guides the alignment, the ungapped blocks of the pair alignments (with the mean matrix score per column as opt) are weighted by the weights of the sequences, the mean number of sequences that have a block at each residue and weightI (--weighti, default 2.7) and added to the match scores of the group-group dynamic program (A__align with constraint 2, no FFT); the matrix of each step is shifted by the offset that the (possibly negative) distance of the step from the tips gives (makedynamicmtx). The pair stage uses its own parameters (globalPairOpen / Offset / Extension = --gop / --gep / --gexp, localPairOpen / Offset / Extension = --lop / --lep / --lexp, genafOpen / genafExtension = --LOP / --LEXP; E-INS: new parameters of 7.243 unless oldGenafParameters). Not available (refused): --retree 0, the memory-saving mode for groups longer than 30 000 columns, the iterative refinement with threads (the installed program gives a different alignment in every run), weightI 0; parttree, add / merge / seed strategies are registered stages of the port. VERIFICATION: rows and standard error equal the installed Debian mafft 7.505-1 on every committed run of scripts/alignment/generate_mafft_progressive_oracle.py (6 530 sets in 28 strategies, at least 210 per strategy: protein and DNA, 3 - 45 sequences, tiny and unrelated sequences, unusual symbols, every option above), of scripts/alignment/generate_mafft_iterative_oracle.py (the iterative refinement, see the counts in B09.md F284) of scripts/alignment/generate_mafft_pairlib_oracle.py (G-INS-1, L-INS-1, E-INS-1: see the counts in B09.md F285), of scripts/alignment/generate_mafft_pairlib_iterative_oracle.py (G-INS-i, L-INS-i, E-INS-i: B09.md F286) and on 884 / 884 pairs (generate_mafft_pair_oracle.py). T-Coffee's mafft_pair uses this port.

sequences.description: Two or more sequences (letters; with anySymbol any character except blanks and '-' is a residue). Like the program: an empty list gives an empty result and ONE sequence is written back (gaps dropped; without anySymbol nucleotides in lower and amino acids in upper case).

offset.description: mafft --ep: offset (default 0.0; a negative value adds to every substitution score, a positive one subtracts).

blosum.description: mafft --bl: BLOSUM matrix of the amino-acid scoring: 30, 45, 50, 62 (default), 80, 90, 100 or 0.

anySymbol.description: true (default): mafft --anysymbol, the original letters are restored in the output. false: the plain command (letters and '.' only; nucleotides lower case, amino acids upper case in the rows).

retree.description: mafft --retree: how many times the guide tree is built (1 = FFT-NS-1, 2 = FFT-NS-2 default, 3; 0 is refused). Two sequences always use 1.

threads.description: mafft --thread (default 0; accepted, no effect on the alignment).

reorder.description: mafft --reorder: the rows in the order of the guide tree.

gapOpenDistance.description: mafft --opdist: gap opening penalty of the distance step (default = gapOpen).

scoringModel.description: 'blosum' (default; mafft --bl), 'jtt' (--jtt / --kimura) or 'tm' (--tm): the scoring matrix of amino acids.

kappa.description: mafft --kappa: transition / transversion ratio of the nucleotide matrix (default: the program's 2).

frequencyModel.description: mafft --fmodel: letter frequencies of the data in the scoring matrix.

wildcardN.description: mafft --nwildcard: n scores like a wildcard in nucleotide sequences.

forceFft.description: mafft --fft given explicitly: the FFT is used for every pair of groups.

terminalGapPenalty.description: mafft --termgappenalty: penalise gaps at the ends.

unweight.description: mafft --unweight: no weighting of the sequences by the guide tree.

maxIterate.description: mafft --maxiterate: cycles of iterative refinement (FFT-NS-i: dndpre distances of the first alignment, then dvtditr refines every branch of the guide tree; the script lets at most 16 run); default 0 = the progressive method. With threads (threads > 0 and threadsIterate not 0) the program is non-deterministic and the call is refused.

threadsIterate.description: mafft --threadit: threads of the iterative step (default: the script's rule min(threads, 8)); 0 = the deterministic single-thread refinement.

pairLibrary.description: 'none' (default: the 6-mer distances of FFT-NS), 'global' (mafft --globalpair, G-INS), 'local' (--localpair, L-INS) or 'genaf' (--genafpair, E-INS): the pairwise alignments of all pairs guide and constrain the progressive alignment (with maxIterate 0 the progressive G-INS-1 / L-INS-1 / E-INS-1, with maxIterate > 0 the iterative G-INS-i / L-INS-i / E-INS-i).

weightI.description: mafft --weighti: weight of the pair library (default 2.7; 0 is refused).

globalPairOpen.description: mafft --gop: gap opening penalty of the global pair alignments (default -2.00).

globalPairOffset.description: mafft --gep: offset of the global pair alignments (default 0.10).

globalPairExtension.description: mafft --gexp: gap extension of the global pair alignments (default -0.10).

localPairOpen.description: mafft --lop: gap opening penalty of the local pair alignments (default -2.00).

localPairOffset.description: mafft --lep: offset of the local pair alignments (default 0.100).

localPairExtension.description: mafft --lexp: gap extension of the local pair alignments (default -0.100).

genafOpen.description: mafft --LOP: the second gap opening penalty of the generalised affine gap costs of 'genaf' (default -6.00).

genafExtension.description: mafft --LEXP: gap extension of the second gap cost of 'genaf' (default -0.000).

oldGenafParameters.description: mafft --oldgenafpair: the parameters of E-INS before 7.243.

format.description: Optional output format; the alignment written in that format is returned in the result field 'formatted'. Biopython Bio.Align names: fasta, a2m, clustal, phylip, nexus, stockholm (byte for byte as Bio.Align.write; 'emboss:' + name selects the EMBOSS writer of the same name). EMBOSS -aformat names: pair, simple, srspair, srs, markx0, markx1, markx2, markx3, markx10, match, score, sam, tcoffee (two rows) and msf, mega, meganon, nexusnon, paup, paupnon, phylipnon, selex, treecon (any number of rows; EMBOSS prints the run date: now, UTC). Omit for no formatted text.

names.description: Optional names of the rows for the formatted output (default seq1, seq2, ...).

alignedSequences.description: The two rows (original letters with --anysymbol, gaps are -).

totalScore.description: Natural affine sum of pairs (BLOSUM62 10 / 0.2 or EDNAFULL 10 / 0.5), rounded; not the program's own score.

formatted.description: The alignment written in the requested format (null when format is omitted).

errors.message: sequences is null, a sequence has no residues, only one sequence, a character above U+007F, or one of = < > with anySymbol
sequenceType is not auto / nuc / amino, blosum is not one of 30 45 50 62 80 90 100 0, gapOpen / offset not finite
NotSupportedException: three or more sequences (the progressive stage is not implemented)
